depth_cohort_timing_deep_panel.note: First passage race for the fear day deepest fifth cohort on the DEEP panel: one expected move is each name's typical range percent times the square root of 20, settled on closes within 60 sessions.

explanation.body: Its forecast takes this form: timing and distribution, over 5, 10, 21 and 60 sessions (cap 60). It is graded on whether its timing calls resolve by each stated horizon, with unresolved cases still counted. It would be ended if after 30 matured cohorts, its timing Brier is no better than the unconditional hazard. It counts as proven at 30 matured cohorts.
explanation.summary: When a defined event gathers a group of stocks, say how long its move is likely to take and which side, up or down, is likely to give way first.

grading_words: Every group is written down at entry, before its first race day opens. It is scored at 5, 10, 21 and 60 trading days on how well its timing chances matched what happened, against the plain past rate for its kind of event. Groups still unsettled at 60 stay in the count as their own outcome.

history.fear_days_set_aside: 17 of the 66 settled fear days produce no group picture: they fall inside the movement recipe's first 22 sessions, when no stock has enough of its own past to measure an expected move, or their day's group is empty; they are counted here, not dropped quietly.
history.words: The pictures above come from replaying each class's own entry rule over the price history on record. That replay is history, computed today; it wrote nothing to the public record. The study corpus behind the design holds 296,093 graded cases, but its per-case rows are not on this disk and its own races stopped at 20 sessions, so the long end of these pictures rests on the shipped history's span alone, and the claim is narrowed to match.

idea: Other pages ask what a move pays. This one asks how long it takes, and which side gives way first. When a defined event gathers a group of stocks (a fear day, a deep-reset group, a wall break, an earnings day, a big gap day), this page writes down, before the race starts, the chance the group's middle stock reaches one expected move up before one expected move down within 5, 10, 21 and 60 trading days, how the waiting time spreads out, and the chance the race settles on each day from 1 to 21.
kill_criterion: After 30 matured groups, if this page's timing score is no better than the plain past rate for the same kind of event, it retires. A group matures when its race settles or at 60 trading days; a group still unsettled at 60 counts as matured, in its own outcome class, never dropped.
